would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The mechanically-checked verdict-shape leg is red: the committed verdict document does not state a status for either chaining mode in a form the check can read.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: verdict-shape is a named 'what must be true' leg of the rubric, and it fails on both modes. The deliverable of this order is a machine- and human-readable verdict per chaining mode at pinned shas; the pipeline arm (ROADMAP Goal 1) and the operator relaying the April thread gate on that per-mode status being legible from the document. A verdict whose per-mode status cannot be read out fails the one thing the document exists to carry, at the moment anyone downstream tries to consume it.

would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: artefacts/docs/ptc-verdict.md:47 ('Summary: 5 passed, 45 failed') vs the per-file block at lines 53-101 — counted: 45 FAIL, 4 PASS, 49 entries.
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The 'verbatim' per-test record of PeTTaChainer's MeTTa suite is incomplete and internally inconsistent with the summary it quotes.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The verdict quotes 'Summary: 5 passed, 45 failed' (50 files) but the per-file block lists 49 entries — 4 PASS and 45 FAIL. One passing test is unaccounted for. suites-verbatim requires the results recorded verbatim per test; a later re-run comparing against this record cannot tell whether a newly-passing test is an upstream fix or the entry that was dropped here, which is exactly the 'still broken vs environment differs' discrimination the verdict is supposed to enable.
